To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the floating-queue technique can be used to solve stochastic network optimization with a finite buffer regime, (b) a floating-queue algorithm is presented that achieves near-optimum utility, (c) the algorithm is shown to achieve a utility-delay-reliablility tradeoff, (d) the floating-queues are shown to achieve the tradeoff with a buffer size that is significantly smaller than existing techniques.

we develop a distributed algorithm for stochastic network optimization with a finite buffer regime that is near-optimal in terms of utility-delay-reliablity tradeoff and that is simple enough to be implemented in practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of distributed algorithms with low complexity and finite buffer size for stochastic network optimization.
the development of a new class of algorithms for stochastic network optimization with a finite buffer regime.
the following open problem: how to implement stochastic network optimization with a finite buffer size?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed floating-queue algorithm is the first distributed algorithm that achieves a near-optimal utility-delay-reliablity tradeoff in stochastic networks with finite buffers.

the floating-queue policy provides the first distributed algorithm that achieves a near-optimal utility with a finite buffer size, a near-optimal per-hop delay, and a near-optimal drop rate in a general stochastic network.
this paper presents the first distributed algorithm that achieves a utility-delay-reliably tradeoff in a finite buffer regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the floating-queue policy achieves near-optimal delay, reliability, and utility performance in a finite buffer regime.
we have proposed an algorithm that is simple, distributed, and achieves the optimal utility-delay-reliablity tradeoff in the finite-buffer regime.
, for the first time, a stochastic network optimization framework can be applied to finite-buffer networks with a small buffer size requirement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a finite buffer size, a network can achieve near-optimal performance with respect to utility, delay, and reliability.
the finite-buffer regime is not necessarily an obstacle for distributed algorithms to achieve near-optimal utility.
the stochastic network optimization paradigm is applicable in a finite-buffer setting.
